chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Samad ibn Muhammad from Hanan from his father from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you enter a town and say, 'I will leave today or tomorrow,' and you have completed ten [days], then complete [the shortened prayer]." This report is to be understood as indicating recommendation (istihbab), based on the evidence of the reports we have previously presented, and what clarifies this further is what he narrated:

key_terms.اسْتَتَمَمْتَ: you have completed (referring to the completion of ten days of travel)
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَاب: recommendation or desirability in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.الْبَلْدَة: a town or city, implying a place of residence or stay
key_terms.فَأَتِمَّ: then complete (referring to performing the full four-rak'ah prayer)

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler's prayer change from shortened to full after entering a town?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the criteria for the 'traveler's prayer' (Salat al-Musafir) when one enters a town with the intent to depart shortly; if ten days of travel have already elapsed, the prayer is performed in full. Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this as a recommended (istihbab) ruling rather than obligatory, highlighting the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on how intention and duration interact to determine prayer length. This reflects the broader principle that the status of a traveler is not solely defined by physical distance but by the continuity of the journey and the stability of residence.
